item.title: Rehost key through a git-ignored xcconfig and Info.plist (#471)
item.body:
Closes #471
Claim: mac/m2-lead

LOT-102 reads `RehostBaseURL` and `RehostAPIKey` from Info.plist, but no build supplied them, so upload stayed off.

Change (ADR 0007, ADR 0012): `App/Config/Shared.xcconfig` (base configuration of the app target, empty defaults, `#include?` of the git-ignored `Secrets.xcconfig`); `App/Config/Info-Keys.plist` merged into the generated Info.plist; `Secrets.xcconfig.example` committed; `.gitignore` entry; App/README section. Base URL `https://img3.super-h.fr` from legacy `ReplyService.swift:2010` (2440d79). No source change.

Checked locally: build with a Secrets.xcconfig gives bundle Info.plist `RehostBaseURL=https://img3.super-h.fr` and a 32-char key; build without the file succeeds with both empty (upload hidden, `configuration(from:)` returns nil). The app launches on the simulator. The panel could not be reached without a logged-in account: see the Mac list. A scan of the diff and of the branch history for the key values found nothing. No upload was sent to any host.

CI needs no secret for tests. For a build that must upload, the maintainer sets Actions secrets `REHOST_BASE_URL` and `REHOST_API_KEY`, and the build job writes them to `App/Config/Secrets.xcconfig`.

Note: the operator's uncommitted local signing edit of `project.pbxproj` will conflict on pull; take both hunks.

Mac check list (device):
- [ ] `App/Config/Secrets.xcconfig` present (copy from the example): build, open the composer, the image panel shows the upload entry (Photos / Camera).
- [ ] Remove the file, clean build: the app builds and the panel shows no upload, manual link still works.
- [ ] With the key, upload one test image to the host the operator agrees to use; the link is inserted; history lists it.
- [ ] The first-use notice names `img3.super-h.fr`.
- [ ] No key in logs or in the Xcode build log.

The app build now supports optional rehost URL and API key settings. Debug and Release use a plist that exposes those settings to the app. The README documents local configuration and CI/release secret requirements. **Changes: Rehost build configuration** |Layer / File(s)|Summary| |:---|:---| |**Define rehost settings and plist keys**
`App/Config/Shared.xcconfig`, `App/Config/Secrets.xcconfig.example`, `.gitignore`, `App/Config/Info-Keys.plist`|`Shared.xcconfig` defines empty defaults and optionally includes `Secrets.xcconfig`. The example documents the rehost URL and API key settings. `.gitignore` excludes the secrets file. The plist maps the settings to `RehostBaseURL` and `RehostAPIKey`.| |**Apply configuration to app builds**
`App/SwiftHFR.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj`, `App/README.md`|Debug and Release use `Shared.xcconfig` and set `INFOPLIST_FILE` to `Config/Info-Keys.plist`. The README describes local configuration and CI/release secret requirements.| **Estimated code review effort:** 2 (Simple) | ~10 minutes **Change:** Bug fix · **Severity of issue fixed:** Medium
Merge Risk: Low · up to e4285

CI-built apps cannot enable image uploads even when the Actions secrets are configured. Add a trusted secret-enabled build path or accept this limitation.
Security architecture risk: Low · up to e4285

Configured builds can now upload images to an external host using an embedded API key. Missing configuration safely disables uploads, and the existing first-use notice and network controls remain in place. No introduced security defect was established, but production credential permissions and release configuration remain unverified. **Retained concerns** No architecture-level concerns identified.
Security review details

**Security Blast Radius** - _inferred_ — Anyone obtaining a configured app bundle can recover its embedded key. Potential reuse reaches the image-host authority granted to that credential, not merely one app user's uploads. Provider permissions and restrictions were not supplied, so administrative, cross-user, or broader service access cannot be asserted or excluded. **Trust Boundaries and Controls** - _observed_ — The existing client requires HTTPS except for loopback HTTP, rejects base-URL credentials, query strings and fragments, uses anonymous transport, disables redirects, and sanitizes credential-bearing diagnostics. It accepts arbitrary valid HTTPS hosts; destination selection is therefore entrusted to build configuration rather than a runtime allowlist. - _observed_ — First-use acceptance precedes image preparation and transmission, and refusal drops the pending image. The notice identifies the configured host and public-image consequences. Acceptance is a device-wide boolean rather than destination-bound consent; that implementation predates this PR, and no host-change rollout was evidenced. **Resilience and Maintainability Implications** - _observed_ — History removal is explicitly local: confirmation explains that the public image remains online. Configuration rollback or local history cleanup is therefore not represented as remote-image deletion. **Hardening Proposals** - _proposed_ — If releases may change hosting destinations, bind remembered acceptance to the approved destination or notice version and require renewed acceptance after a change. This addresses a conditional future transition, not an established bypass in this rollout. - _proposed_ — For releases intended to enable uploads, verify the archived destination and credential presence without printing the key, and confirm with the host operator that the distributed credential has appropriate permissions, quotas and rotation arrangements.

REHOST_BASE_URL = https:/$()/img3.super-h.fr -REHOST_API_KEY = your-chevereto-api-key +REHOST_API_KEY = ```

> **IMPORTANT** > Review the replacement and indentation, then test before committing. ```suggestion REHOST_API_KEY = ```
